      node.style.top = '5px';

      range.selectNodeContents(node);
      selection.addRange(range);

      selection.removeAllRanges();
      return Promise.resolve();
    }

        // eslint-disable-next-line flowtype/no-flow-fix-me-comments

        return navigator.clipboard.writeText(text);
      }

      if (!body) {

      }

      const node = createNode(text);
      body.appendChild(node);
      copyNode(node);
      body.removeChild(node);
      return Promise.resolve();
    }

      const id = button.getAttribute('for');
      const text = button.getAttribute('value');

      function trigger() {

      }

      const img = document.createElement("img");
      const doc = parser.parseFromString(svg, "image/svg+xml");
      const svgEl = doc.querySelector("svg");
      const { maxWidth } = svgEl?.style || {};
      const firstTitle = doc.querySelector("title");
      const firstDesc = doc.querySelector("desc");

      img.setAttribute("src", `data:image/svg+xml,${encodeURIComponent(svg)}`);
      if (maxWidth) {
        img.width = parseInt(maxWidth);
      }
      if (firstTitle) {
        img.setAttribute("alt", firstTitle.textContent);
      }
      if (firstDesc) {
        const caption = document.createElement("figcaption");
        caption.className = "sr-only";
        caption.textContent = firstDesc.textContent;
        return [img, caption];
      }
      return [img];
    }

    async function makeMermaidError(text) {
      let errorMessage = "";
      try {
        await mermaid.parse(text);
      } catch (err) {
        errorMessage = `${err}`;
      }

      const result = document.createElement("details");
      result.className = 'jp-RenderedMermaid-Details';
      const summary = document.createElement("summary");
      summary.className = 'jp-RenderedMermaid-Summary';
      const pre = document.createElement("pre");
      const code = document.createElement("code");
      code.innerText = text;
      pre.appendChild(code);
      summary.appendChild(pre);
      result.appendChild(summary);

      const warning = document.createElement("pre");
      warning.innerText = errorMessage;
      result.appendChild(warning);
      return [result];
    }

      const id = `jp-mermaid-${_nextMermaidId++}`;

      el.style.visibility = "hidden";

        results.map(output.appendChild, output);
      } catch (err) {
        parent.classList.add("jp-mod-warning");
        results = await makeMermaidError(raw);
        output = results[0];
      } finally {
        el.remove();
      }
      parent.classList.add("jp-RenderedMermaid");
      parent.appendChild(output);
    }


    /**
     * Post-process to ensure mermaid diagrams contain only valid SVG and XHTML.
     */
    function cleanMermaidSvg(svg) {
      return svg.replace(RE_VOID_ELEMENT, replaceVoidElement);
    }


    /**
     * A regular expression for all void elements, which may include attributes and
     * a slash.
     *
     * @see https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/Void_element
     *
     * Of these, only `<br>` is generated by Mermaid in place of `\n`,
     * but _any_ "malformed" tag will break the SVG rendering entirely.
     */
    const RE_VOID_ELEMENT =
      /<\s*(area|base|br|col|embed|hr|img|input|link|meta|param|source|track|wbr)\s*([^>]*?)\s*>/gi;

    /**
     * Ensure a void element is closed with a slash, preserving any attributes.
     */
    function replaceVoidElement(match, tag, rest) {
      rest = rest.trim();
      if (!rest.endsWith('/')) {
        rest = `${rest} /`;
      }
      return `<${tag} ${rest}>`;

<h1 id="recovering-progression-constraints-with-treemhn">Recovering progression constraints with TreeMHN<a class="anchor-link" href="#recovering-progression-constraints-with-treemhn">¶</a></h1><p>Runs the real <strong><a href="https://github.com/cbg-ethz/TreeMHN">TreeMHN</a></strong> (Luo, Kuipers & Beerenwinkel 2023) on
a cohort simulated by <code>iscc</code>, and checks that it recovers the event-ordering constraints that were
<em>planted</em> when the cohort was grown.</p>
<p><strong>R notebook</strong>, kernel <code>R (iscc-treemhn)</code>, no simulation. Generated once by
<code>python validation/make_analysis_data.py --only treemhn</code>:</p>
<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>file</th>
<th>what it is</th>
<th>who sees it</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>trees.csv</code></td>
<td>one mutation tree per patient, <strong>reconstructed by SCITE</strong>, in TreeMHN's own <code>input_tree_df</code> layout</td>
<td>the tool</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>truth_network.json</code></td>
<td>the planted precedence DAG</td>
<td><strong>scoring only</strong></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p><strong>The trees are inferred, not read.</strong> <code>iscc</code> knows every patient's true tree, and handing that
straight to TreeMHN would make this vacuous — it would be estimating rates from the topology it
is meant to infer. Each patient is genotyped single-cell instead, with dropout and false
positives, and SCITE reconstructs the tree from that noisy matrix.</p>
<p><strong>How to regenerate exactly these trees.</strong> <code>make_analysis_data.py --only treemhn</code> grows the cohort,
then for each patient draws <code>n_cells_sequenced</code> cells in proportion to clone size, corrupts the
genotypes at <code>scite_fd</code> (false positive) and <code>scite_ad</code> (allelic dropout), and runs SCITE on that
matrix with the same rates and a per-patient seed — <code>validation/scite_common.py</code>, one MCMC chain of
100,000 steps. <code>meta.json</code> records the values used, printed below, so the trees are reproducible from
the dataset alone. <a href="tool_scite_trees.ipynb">Tree reconstruction from single-cell DNA with SCITE</a>
shows what that step looks like and scores it against the true genotypes.</p>
<p><strong>The question.</strong> Real cohort data has no answer key — you cannot tell whether a recovered dependency
is real. Here <code>iscc</code> grew every patient under a <em>known</em> DAG saying which events must precede which, so
recovery is measurable.</p>
<p>Two details make this a fair test rather than a trivial one, and both were learned the hard way:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>The constraints are <code>accessibility</code>-gated</strong>, meaning they act on the mutation process itself, so
the ordering genuinely appears in tree topology — the observable TreeMHN reads. (iscc can also gate
the <em>same</em> DAG on fitness, where it changes only how large the carrying clones grow and leaves no
ordering trace. TreeMHN estimates rates, so it recovers nothing from that — a real finding, but a
statement about observables rather than about the tool, and it belongs in the benchmark suite.)</li>
<li><strong>The event alphabet is common enough for a gated child to occur.</strong> A child cannot appear until its
parent has, so with rare events it arises in almost no patient and there is nothing in the data to
find, however good the method.</li>
</ul>
</div>

<div class="clipboard-copy-txt" id="cell-1">source("r_preamble.R")
suppressMessages({ library(TreeMHN); library(jsonlite) })

data_dir <- analysis_dir("treemhn")
df    <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "trees.csv"))
truth <- fromJSON(file.path(data_dir, "truth_network.json"))

n        <- max(df$Mutation_ID)          # number of real events (the root is 0)
patients <- unique(df$Patient_ID)
dag <- truth$true_dag_edges              # rows: (parent, child), 0-based event ids

meta <- fromJSON(file.path(data_dir, "meta.json"))
cat(sprintf("cohort: %d patients, %d events, %d tree rows\n", length(patients), n, nrow(df)))
cat(sprintf("trees from: %s  (%d cells/patient, false positive %.3f, dropout %.2f)\n",
            meta$trees_from, meta$n_cells_sequenced, meta$scite_fd, meta$scite_ad))
cat(sprintf("gating: %s   planted precedence constraints: %d\n",
            truth$dependency_params$gating_mode, nrow(dag)))
for (i in seq_len(nrow(dag)))
  cat(sprintf("   E%d  must precede  E%d\n", dag[i, 1], dag[i, 2]))</div>

<h2 id="scoring-against-the-planted-constraints">Scoring against the planted constraints<a class="anchor-link" href="#scoring-against-the-planted-constraints">¶</a></h2><p>In an MHN, <code>Theta[i, j]</code> is the effect of event <em>j</em> on event <em>i</em>'s rate — positive means <em>j</em> promotes
<em>i</em>. A planted "<em>p</em> must precede <em>c</em>" constraint should therefore surface as a <strong>large positive
<code>Theta[c, p]</code></strong>.</p>
<p>So the test is not whether Θ looks plausible, but whether the planted pairs are the <em>top-ranked</em>
promoting entries out of all off-diagonals.</p>
</div>

<div class="clipboard-copy-txt" id="cell-3">off_idx <- which(row(Theta) != col(Theta), arr.ind = TRUE)
off_val <- Theta[off_idx]
ord     <- order(off_val, decreasing = TRUE)

# planted (parent, child) -> the Theta entry that should carry it: Theta[child, parent]
planted <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(dag)), function(i) c(child = dag[i, 2] + 1L, parent = dag[i, 1] + 1L))

cat("TreeMHN vs the planted DAG\n")
ranks <- integer(0)
for (pc in planted) {
  hit <- which(off_idx[ord, "row"] == pc["child"] & off_idx[ord, "col"] == pc["parent"])
  ranks <- c(ranks, hit)
  cat(sprintf("  E%d -> E%d :  Theta = %+.3f   rank %d of %d off-diagonal entries\n",
              pc["parent"] - 1L, pc["child"] - 1L,
              Theta[pc["child"], pc["parent"]], hit, length(off_val)))
}
cat(sprintf("\n  both planted edges in the top %d of %d  ->  %s\n",
            max(ranks), length(off_val),
            ifelse(max(ranks) <= nrow(dag), "RECOVERED (they are the top entries)",
                   ifelse(max(ranks) <= length(off_val) / 3, "recovered (top third)", "not recovered"))))
cat("\nstrongest off-diagonals overall:\n")
top <- head(ord, 4)
for (k in top)
  cat(sprintf("   E%d -> E%d : %+.3f\n", off_idx[k, "col"] - 1L, off_idx[k, "row"] - 1L, off_val[k]))</div>

<h2 id="the-contrast-the-same-cohort-read-cross-sectionally">The contrast: the same cohort read cross-sectionally<a class="anchor-link" href="#the-contrast-the-same-cohort-read-cross-sectionally">¶</a></h2><p>TreeMHN reads <strong>mutation trees</strong>, which carry the order in which each patient acquired its events.
Classical <strong>MHN</strong> (Schill et al. 2020) reads only a <strong>binary presence matrix</strong> — "did this patient ever
acquire event <em>i</em>" — which is what a cross-sectional or bulk cohort gives you, and which discards order
entirely.</p>
<p><code>make_analysis_data.py</code> writes both views of these same patients, so the comparison isolates what the
extra resolution of trees buys. MHN is a Python package, so it gets its own notebook and its own
kernel rather than being shelled out to from here.</p>
